question: In the management of acute iridocyclitis, a cycloplegic agent such as atropine is prescribed primarily to prevent posterior synechiae formation and to relieve painful ciliary muscle spasm.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Cycloplegics (atropine, cyclopentolate) are essential in iridocyclitis management for two reasons — preventing posterior synechiae by keeping the pupil dilated, and relieving painful ciliary spasm. Steroid drops address the inflammation itself; cycloplegics address the structural and pain consequences.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Cycloplegics serve two simultaneous purposes in iridocyclitis: (1) they dilate the pupil, preventing adhesion of the inflamed iris to the anterior lens capsule (posterior synechiae); and (2) they paralyse the ciliary muscle, relieving the spasm that causes deep, aching pain. This dual rationale is a frequent examination point.
